changes.evidence: A long independent line runs beneath multiplicité, crossing the descending p but continuing below the other letters. H does not mark the visible underline.
After the separately written de the first low loop is heavily retraced and the terminal low return may be e or n. Keep ce preferred with en admitted; the earlier extra-de decision remains unchanged.

The left large open return and closed upright loop can form a flourished O, followed by a low n under two cancellation strokes. The blind alternative (les is possible if the left return is a parenthesis and the loop an l. The crossing conceals the small following letters; retain On first but no longer assert certainty. Et above is a separate live replacement.

The replacement is raised above the struck voit que, so its insertion state must be explicit. After r/e/g/a/r and tall d the low return and small rising hook followed by a detached round point favor regarder.; compressed o/n/s may still account for that ending, so regardons remains an alternative. No separate on is visible.

After alpha the first tall stem descends and has a right shoulder like p; the next small turn, detached dot and final curved s favor pris. A crossed or retraced f/i/x/é sequence with possible final s remains possible. Record pris first with fixés and fixé; singular grammar does not select the reading.
The word has two looped d forms, low intervening vowels, an i-dot, a crossed t and the final e return, followed by a separate comma. These strokes do not spell disons.

Between comme and pour is the longer t-a-n-t-o-t sequence: an initial tall t, the extended low middle, another raised/crossed member, and a terminal t. It is longer than tout. The crop clips part of the upper ascenders, so the circumflex is not treated as absent; the accent remains explicitly uncertain and the second-reading box extends upward.

The ending has a tall crossed f-like form with a long descending return. It is heavily retraced and crossed below the line, so the final state is not fully recoverable. Relatif remains the preferred reading, with relative retained; no independent extra word is supplied for H’s trailing illegible placeholder.

The subscript has a tall narrow curved body and lower return before small alpha. Its height favors S, but the blind lowercase s remains plausible in this compressed hand, so retain both cases rather than assert a mathematical distinction.

The word before the cancellation ends in a small downward return after the long e stroke, supporting the final s of des. The abbreviation that follows is separately read as pt.; the written determiner is not normalized to match it.

The tall t and i-dot remain visible, but the horizontal cancellation covers most of the following low letters. A low final trace is compatible with plural sections, but a separate final s cannot be established securely. C’s plural is retained as the preferred reading and H’s singular as an alternative.
The live abbreviation has one p descender, a small raised crossed t and a separate low point. There is no intervening s between t and the point.
The next manuscript row begins directly with the short rat. and then sur k(s_alpha). There is no spelled-out rationnel or intervening on a un pt. between the preceding live pt. and this rat.
The main letter after de has two tall arms joined by an open lower basin: U, not the crossing diagonals of X. Its small subscript is retraced; the s/S case remains unresolved.
After the dash are two low separated word groups with a detached apostrophe over the latter. They read on n’a, not the dotted abbreviation i.e.
The following row begins with a q loop and long descender, followed by the low u, apostrophe and un. The initial qu’ is written.

Between pt and the tall l are two separated small marks one above the other, with no a bowl or joining stroke. Keep a colon as written. The following l’apostrophe and dotted i/n/f/i/n/i are unchanged.
The point formula ends with its comma, and the next base-text row starts rat sur k_alpha. No second i.e. qui est à l’infini clause is written there; the actual à l’infini occurs before the formula.
The small t after r/a has its cross-stroke but no separate following abbreviation point before sur. The period farther right belongs after the field expression, not after rat.

After the final long f descender are two detached vertically separated points, followed by cet. There is no connecting a bowl. Keep the colon rather than expand the sign to à.

second_boxes.reading:
qu’un pt à l’infini $i_\alpha\in X_{s_\alpha}\setminus U_{s_\alpha}$,
\inserted{maintenant}

$L_i\subset\pi$ relatif à cet $i_\alpha$, justement,
de façon ess. canonique,

notes:
This leaf first identifies the quantity discussed in the preceding continuation with the multiplicity along a divisor component D_alpha. It then asks what happens for points on the union of those components, fixes one alpha, and describes an extension attached to the generic point of that component and a suitable open subset. In this situation the text says that there are no longer rational points of the generic curve of the earlier kind, but a rational point at infinity i_alpha; it then refers to a subgroup L_i of pi attached to that point in an essentially canonical fashion. The final comma continues the discussion. This summarizes the page’s statements without asserting that they have been proved or checked.
Visual review: the whole sheet and both full-resolution halves were viewed once. The first bottom-half tool call failed before displaying the image; the successful retry was the single actual bottom-half view. Every word, formula, abbreviation, index, sign, cancellation, insertion and underline was compared against both witnesses. Fifteen saved crops were inspected once, with no recropping. The crops use the original boxes recorded here, grayscale autocontrast, LANCZOS resizing to 2200 pixels width and sharpening. No OCR, text recognition, external research, or other leaf was consulted. The sheet contains twenty prose rows including the compressed last row, no diagram or drawing, no visible author page number at its head, and the separate folio 93 at bottom left.
Reading decisions: the extra de after donc, inserted et, déduite and the absence of an added pour before alpha are retained. Completed adjudication leaves ce|en, cancelled On|(les, raised regarder.|regardons, inline alpha pris|fixés|fixé and the earlier U_Salpha|U_salpha doubtful. The later point phrase has a literal colon: on n’a qu’un pt : l’infini. Multiplicité is underlined. The live abbreviation before rat. is pt., not C’s pts.; no s lies between the small raised t and its following point. Des is retained as written. The deleted sections/section remains uncertain under its strike. The point at infinity formula and the curved leader place maintenant after dispose, not before rat. The later rat has no abbreviation point. De façon remains live: the local horizontal stroke belongs to the f crossbar rather than a phrase-wide cancellation.
The adjective ending remains relatif|relative because its f-like descender is heavily retraced. In the later U expression, U itself is clear against H’s X, but the s/S subscript remains overworked. The field expression retains its uncertain k/K and lower alpha, together with a separately recorded xi-like form and raised point to their right. Adjudication does not establish a cancellation layer there. The long word after comme is tantot rather than tout. The first crop clipped part of the upper ascenders; completed adjudication of the expanded second-reading box still leaves the faint upper trace insufficient to settle a circumflex, so tantôt|tantot remains. The point-at-infinity second box likewise extends upward to include the complete upper part of the formula. In that box maintenant is shown on its separate physical line; its actual attachment after dispose is given in the insertion box and full draft. No author question mark is added. Font/macro conventions such as E versus mathcal E are not counted as reading changes.
Mathematical checks: no independent proof, computation, mathematical use or refutation was performed. The content summary above describes the manuscript, and the stroke comparisons are visual checks only. check_events remains empty. No compilation was performed.

Blind adjudication supersedes the first-stage certainty about On, regardons, fixé and the capital subscript S. The raised replacement is now regarder.|regardons, with the detached end point favoring the first. Alpha is followed by pris|fixés|fixé, chosen from stroke shapes rather than grammar. Both former à readings at pt ... l’infini and relatif ... cet are two detached vertical points and are retained as colons. The field expression also contains a xi-like form and raised point to the right of k_alpha, now explicitly retained under doubt. The generic-fibre subscript remains s/S: no independent opening and closing parentheses support the blind k(s_alpha) alternative. Pt. remains singular because its t is followed directly by an isolated point. All thirteen differing boxes were inspected.
